exposure: mode of delivery (caesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
timing of prophylactic antibiotics for caesarean section (pre-incision vs post-cord clamping)
in-utero exposure to antibiotics immediately prior to birth
cohort: Children born in the UK during 2006-18 delivered by caesarean section (compared to a control cohort delivered vaginally)
finding: There was no evidence that the policy change from post-cord clamping to pre-incision prophylactic antibiotics for caesarean sections during 2006-18 had an impact on the incidence of asthma and eczema in early childhood in the UK.
mod_finding: The study investigated the impact of changing the timing of prophylactic antibiotics for cesarean sections from post-cord clamping to pre-incision on childhood asthma and eczema rates.
